questions.answer: Difficult to find a place, where you didn't have to sign a 1-year lease.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
In Norway: Make a "leietaker" profil at
Hybel.no
. That is the best way to find housing off campus.

Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: At Studentweb you had to register your courses and sign up for the exams.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could call or email NTNU if you had any questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Partly successful. Unfortunately I couldn't get one of the courses I wanted the most, due to overlapping exam with one course and overlapping field course with another course.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Even though I had a pre-approval for more courses than I needed, I still had to make a new pre-approval because the timeschedule of the courses didn't fit each other. Due to that reason I would advise future exchange student to get a pre-approval for even more ECTS than your backup plan needs.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of courses was good.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was the same. There was a couple of lectures during the week, and the same amount of reading. Though was there not any "øvelsestimer", as there is at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: POL2024 and BI2081. They were very good and informative.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: NTNU has an amazing offer of social and athletic activities. All kinds of sport is being offered at a very student friendly price. I myself did hiphop and breakdance classes.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: A would recommend to join Sit idret, which is a part of NTNU. Here you can join all kinds of sports classes.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: If you are interested in outdoor experiences, I would recommend going to Jotunheimen Nationalpark, Romsdalen and Røros. NTNU also has a lot of cabins you can rent. That is a very good way to spend your weekends.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the some of the classes at Sit. I met a lot of local students at my dance classes.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I don't think there was cultural differences.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The outdoor and cabin culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Trondheim is an amazing student city. There is so many offers to students through NTNU. Explore the "hyttekultur" and join a Sit class. If you are to find housing on your own, don't sign a 1-year lease. It is easy to find housing in Trondheim when you get there, just use
Hybel.no
.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting other exchange students and going on cabin trips and outdoor trips with them. Getting to know other cultures.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I had a very unpleasant situation with my landlord. Luckily everything worked out in the end.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
